title: Backflow device identification: record the model, type, and size
description: Reliable identification combines the full assembly photo, manufacturer label, model, nominal size, system use, and location.
prompt: What evidence identifies this device well enough for service or testing?
answer: Reliable identification combines the full assembly photo, manufacturer label, model, nominal size, system use, and location. Shape alone is not enough to select parts, testing, or replacement.
urgency: Escalate unreadable labels, conflicting records, a failed test, or a part request without model confirmation.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: The label and size are the primary identity record.
System use and location provide context but do not replace manufacturer data.
A serial number may help asset tracking but is not always a parts lookup key.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Verify the exact asset
steps.body: Photograph the label and full installation before a service visit.

steps.title: Apply the right requirement
steps.body: Match the label to manufacturer literature and the asset record.

steps.title: Retain the completed record
steps.body: Use verified identity to route to the correct test, repair, or replacement path.

safeChecks: Use the official utility or authority requirement for this property.
Confirm exact model and size before parts, repair, or replacement work.
Retain the final result with the property asset record.
stopConditions: The model or size cannot be confirmed.
The device family is being guessed from a visual resemblance.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
evidenceNote: The governing program determines compliance requirements, while exact manufacturer documentation determines the identified assembly service path.
